label: step 3-4 of short sequences: <DEL> when L<=4, or 4th original token (o/a/u/r/q/d)
explanation: Fires only at absolute steps 0, 3 and 4, never in the copy phase. Most mass (57%) is on the <DEL> step of short sequences: L=3 delimiter fires 83% of the time (40% of mass, largest activations, especially when the prefix contains s/t/z/p/h, e.g. "2 s t <DEL>"), L=4 delimiter fires 17% of the time. The rest is the 4th original token (t=3) in longer sequences, preferring o, a, u, r, q, d as input and boosted when s/t/z/p/h appeared earlier. Also tiny activations (~0.02 of max) on input o at t=0, which are missed. Does not fire at t=1, t>=5, or on <DEL> for L>=5. Predicate captures ~91% of mass but precision is low (~24%) because which t=3 tokens fire depends on the prefix in a way I could not reduce to a simple rule.
